To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IGF-I and IGF-II can induce GVBD in MIS-incompetent oocytes and that the IGF-I-induced GVBD is independent of the steroidogenic pathways.

IGF-I is a more potent stimulator of in vitro oocyte maturation than IGF-II in the striped bass, and that IGF-I stimulates oocyte maturation in a manner that requires protein synthesis, but does not require MIS production, gap junctional communication or follicle steroidogenesis.
IGF-I induces GVBD via MIS-independent and transcription-independent pathways, but requires protein translation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the insulin-like growth factors (IGF) and their receptors (IGFR) in ovarian physiology of teleosts.
the effects of IGF-I on oocyte maturation in vitro and ovarian steroidogenesis in striped bass.
the role(s) of IGF-I and other factors in the regulation of oocyte meiosis and ovarian steroidogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

IGF-I is the most important factor in the regulation of oocyte maturation in striped bass, but that the mechanism of IGF-I action is complex and involves both transcription-dependent and -independent processes.
rhIGF-I is a potent inducer of GVBD, but that it is not the endogenous maturation-inducing factor.
IGF-I and IGF-II can induce GVBD and steroidogenesis in vitro in striped bass oocytes, but IGF-I is more potent and more effective than IGF-II in this species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IGF-I induces final oocyte maturation in striped bass, a process that is coupled to ovarian steroidogenesis.
IGF-I induces in vitro GVBD in striped bass oocytes via a transcription-dependent pathway that requires protein synthesis.
rhIGF-I induces oocyte maturation via a mechanism that involves steroid production and is not coupled to the follicle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IGF-I is a potent maturation-inducing factor in fish oocytes and is a potential target for manipulation of oocyte maturation and ovulation in aquaculture species.
IGF-I is a potent inducer of GVBD, which is not coupled to steroidogenesis.
